payload.body:
**ONE CALL WANTED, AND IT IS A NEW DEFECT FOUND WHILE REVIEWING 0085 -- does it get an issue now, with the lighthouse at two, or does it wait?** Everything else here is a report. (AC-3.2 from 21:19Z is still with you and unrelated to this.)

**A WRAPPER FLAG TYPED AT A COMMAND-LEVEL GATE IS HANDED TO THE TOOL AS AN ARGUMENT, AND THE GATE DOES NOT DO WHAT WAS ASKED.** Measured, one fixture project declaring the same `run: echo hello` twice, once as a gated option and once as a gated command:

- `devbin probe gated --purge` -- tool argv is `echo hello`, and the run reports `purged 0 old run file(s) ... keeping the newest 5`. Correct.
- `devbin sealed --purge` -- tool argv is `echo hello --purge`, the run prints `hello --purge`, **and no purge happens at all.** No warning, no refusal.

`--purge-only` and `--allow-empty` take the same path. `--allow-empty` is the one that matters most: it is the corpus's explicit per-invocation "this emptiness is intended" override, so at a command-level gate an operator asking for it gets neither the override nor a refusal -- they get a corrupted command line and a gate that still fails.

**THIS IS NOT A NEW CLASS. IT IS THE EXACT DEFECT `gate_split_args` WAS WRITTEN TO END, RECURRING AT A SITE ADDED AFTERWARDS.** That function's own header says so: it exists because "`test mix --purge` asked mix to run a file called --purge", ruled back in by you on 2026-08-09, and it claims **"ONE parser, used by BOTH gate call sites -- gatecmd's `run_builtin_gate` and `run_option`'s declared-gate branch -- so the two paths cannot drift on what counts as a wrapper flag."**

**There are THREE call sites.** `gate_split_args` is called at `lib/gatecmd:100` and `lib/resolve:771` and nowhere else; `DEVBIN_GATE_FLAGS` is passed at `gatecmd:140`, `gatecmd:161` and `resolve:777`, and not at `resolve:915`. The command-level gate was added later, and the comment that guaranteed no drift was never re-read against it. **A Highlander claim written as a promise rather than as a test is how the third site got in without anyone noticing** -- nothing compared the sites, so nothing reported the third.

**THE FALSE COMMENT SITS DIRECTLY ABOVE IT, and it is why I went looking.** `lib/resolve:894` says a command-level gate "seals on exactly the terms an option-level one does (D19)". It does not. dc's 0085 edits that very comment to add "the source line is one of those terms and was missing until issue 0085" -- true, and it now implies the other terms were audited. **A comment that has just been corrected is the most trusted comment in the file**, so 0085 makes the remaining falsehood harder to find rather than easier. I have told dc to have the amendment name the wrapper flags as a known remaining difference.

**WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: I have not filed it and I have not fixed it.** Directive 2 says issues for maintenance-class work, so the shape is clear, but decision 29 has us closing every open issue and the count is two -- so a third appearing tonight is yours to want or not. Three ways it can go, my recommendation first:

1. **File it now, unclaimed, and let it sit past the lighthouse.** The defect is silent and live in every estate running a command-level gate, and the finding is measured and written; losing it to a session boundary costs more than the count does. It does not have to be worked tonight.
2. File it and fix it tonight. Cheap on the face of it -- `gate_split_args "$@"` plus the flags array at the third site -- but it changes what a command-level gate does with its argv, which is the fleet's blast radius, and I would not do that at this hour on a green tree.
3. Hold it in my board and file it after the lighthouse. My objection to this is that a board is not where a fleet defect keeps.

**0085 IS NOT CLOSED AND THAT IS ON MY REVIEW, NOT ON dc.** Its code is right at all six sites. Its coverage is not: the class arm asserts the `--source` flag is PRESENT while `note_invocation` prints the provenance line only when the VALUE is non-empty, so `--source ""` at fullcycle or the test handler restores 0085's own defect and survives every arm. dc found that by attacking its own work and said so before I got there, which is the right instinct and is on the record. I drove the discriminating pair on the landed bytes -- the identical mutation dies at the command-level site, which has a behavioural arm, and survives at both sites that have none -- and disproved the one sentence of dc's fix plan that said fullcycle cannot be driven: it can, with a `DEVBIN_LIB` shim, no full cycle executed, and I sent the working recipe. dc's six mutants re-drive to its matrix exactly. Four items are back with dc; nothing here needs you.

**Where things stand.** Open: 0064 and 0085. ST0007 WP-03's six AT rows are minted and `to-write`, nothing in `lib/` written, AC-3.2 awaiting your ruling. `intent organize --apply` still held on your call, 28 files. Nothing pushed. No full suite run by me tonight -- single-file runs in a detached worktree, removed after, so your EOD suite was never touched.
